children: Arabica coffee futures eased toward $3 per pound, reaching their lowest since late June, pressured by expectations of higher output from top producer Brazil.
According to Safras & Mercado, the Brazilian harvest for the 2026/27 season was 97% complete as of August 26, with Arabica variety at 96%, with the country heading for a potential record crop.
Supporting this view, Rabobank said in a quarterly report that it still expects a “very comfortable” global coffee balance in 2026/27, with a surplus of 8.9 million bags.
However, the bank noted that harvest delays in Brazil and problems stemming from the earthquake in Colombia are keeping  stocks tight for now, with significant replenishment unlikely before November.
Arabica coffee stocks monitored by ICE continued to fall, reaching 223,976 bags by August 31, the lowest level in 27 years.

title: Arabica Coffee Futures at Over 2-Month Low
